I can not give this game a positive review in conscience of the level of unpolished the design of it gets during the higher difficulties. I like a lot about this game on Normal, it isn’t totally remarkable, but it has some decent highs, but the lows of it get noticeably escalated on Old School and to an unholy amount on Hard as Balls. 


A game shouldn’t boil down to how fast you can give yourself arthritis because the developer didn’t care to add an autofire, or at least not up the general enemy health so you can strain yourself. I have some criticisms to give about Dark Onward as Area 52’s boss and the insanity of having nearly no way to escape the rockets at the final phase, but that’s honestly something you would have to see or play for yourself before I explained it in depth.   


The gimmick of Virtual Insanity, the last level before the final boss is that it’s intentionally hard to look at, and the red and black palette makes certain enemies blend in. Your view is also obscured quite a bit, and it makes learning the obstacles harder, there’s some leeway but a lot of players will only learn it by pure muscle memory since the skill involved isn’t conventional unlike the first game’s final level.


The final boss requires unconventional precision and needs you to spam the fire button to its max for the enemies it spawns out. It creates for a unique challenge, but that factor shouldn’t exist at all.




These moments make for Hard as Balls (And the last difficulty mode which I haven’t tried as of writing this) to be a miserable experience just by them alone. These problems wouldn’t happen in a well balanced game. Its predecessor is bad about it too and is worse considering that you need to beat the entire game with annoyingly tough enemies with one life, and one health point with zero continues to get all of the achievements for it.

I played the first one on my 3DS when I saw this game on one of the AVGN episodes by James Rolfe. His sereis is the main reason why I like playing retro video games. After playing this game for 2 hours here's my review of the game. You start off in your home with your nes zapper shooting enemies that get in your way. You can get upgrades like the cape that lets you glide for a few seconds, power glove that can break through brick walls, super scope that does more damage, a upgrade that can charge your shots for more damage, a gaming helmet that can let you see hidden blocks, and others. You need to get 6 green triforce stars to make it to the last level. Getting the upgrades can help you out in bosses. Some are hidden but I used a guide to help me out. You fight bosses you might be familiar with like the Nostalgia Critic. When you go idle for a few seconds AVGN gives you the finger. The music in this game is pretty good for a old school inspired game. Some levels were tough for me like those death blocks that can insta kill you or enemies that can one shot you when you get nera them like the chainsaw dudes. You go through different levels like Area 52, a Japan inspired level, board land, sewers, black and white place with ghost, and monsters, and the tutorial level which is AVGN's home. Every level you blow up the level with a bomb killing all the area. You can side items like f bombs that explode when they hit something, steel balls that are used to damage enemies, beer keg that can heal up all your health, and others. Each last level of a stage you fight a boss which was easy for me since I played it on easy diffculty. There are references to James Rolfe's friend and characters from his other shows. There's even reference's to old video games and cartoons like Totaro from my Neighbor Totaro. Even had parts where the game lagged on me like in the sewer level but was normal after a few minutes. I did have a few problems with the game like not being able to use my Xbox One controller properly for this game. I tried to configure the buttons and that didn't help. There are collectables like getting all the nerd letters but stopped after a while because I didn't feel like getting them. If you want to get this game wait untli there's a sale and you can get both games for a good price. I give this game a 8 out of 10.

As a fan of the Angry Video Game Nerd, who also loved the first game, AVGN Adventures, this is a really good follow up with new power-ups, more levels, and more callbacks to the web series. Each stage is split up into 3 acts and a boss fight, similar to a Sonic game, and their all laid out on a map, just like Super Mario World. In each world, there's one of the Nerd's NES Accessories hidden in one act or another; and just like Mega Man X, you have to find one accessory, then use it to find the other in a different stage, which adds more exploration, while not being too cryptic. 

The game also feels like a celebration of other Cinemassacre properties like "Monster Madness" and "Board James", both of which came with their own unique level designs and mechanics for their respective stages. They even pay respects to the AVGN Movie, while simultaneously satirizing movie-based games that aren't faithful adaptations in the first place! XD 

If there are a few small issues, I don't like how they got rid of the other playable characters (i.e. Guitar Guy, Mike, and B.S Man). I guess because the power-ups had the same abilities? However, the unlockable characters in the first game still made certain platforming challenges and boss fights a lot easier and encouraged different ways of playing the game, so it's sad to see them gone. Also, did anyone else notice that the Nerd's running speed is a bit slower? I couldn't help but feel like movement was a little less precise in this one. Also, while the pixelated graphics look good, the blum effect comes off as over-saturated in this game, which sometimes makes the picture quality a bit blurry; it's almost as bad as the original Twilight Princess.

But these are very small issues in an otherwise awesome, challenging platformer that anyone can pick up and play! Check it out if you wanna be taken back to the past! ;)

Graphics:

Angry Video Game Nerd 2 looks pretty close to how the first game looked (which looked great), but now the graphics are crispier and the environments are also really good. You visit a few locations themed after the games the Nerd has covered in the past like Hong Kong 97 and TMNT.

Each world is quite different from one another and there's tons of enemy variety quite a few of them being exclusive to that specific world you're trying to finish at the moment. There's a lot more detail now too, it feels like a ton of effort went into making each world incredibly detailed with unique looking levels, even when you're still visiting the same world. 

Audio:

First of all I have to start off with the soundtrack, which was a great highlight in the first game. I was really surprised with the music for the first game and I was anticipating hearing the track list for the sequel and I was at first slightly disappointed. The soundtrack is by no means bad, but it's nowhere near as good as the first games music, there's still quite a few really good tracks that are really catchy and provide as nice backdrop for the levels.

However one thing from the first game has returned and that's the sound effects that stack on top of each other. So for example when you kill someone they explode and make a sound, so when many things going on, it really feels like an attack on your senses. This was a big problem in the first one, especially on the flying levels and it was toned down in the sequel, but not fully removed. 

Gameplay:

The gameplay in AVGN 2 is by far the biggest improvement over the first game and I'm glad to say that it felt much more fun to play because of it. So first of all let's cover the gameplay. AVGN 2 is a side scrolling shooter where you're going from left to right all while gunning down enemies and doing some platforming. Now you have a few new additions to the gameplay like a wall jump and power ups it feels a lot more fluid. 

First of all, let's cover the thing that the first game has become notorious for, the level design. The first games level design is pretty bad as most levels have artificial difficulty by placing copious amounts of death blocks, which are a one hit kill if you touch them. 2 while doesn't remove them entirely, they use them much more sparingly and honestly the level design overall feels much better overall. It feels like they actually took time off to make levels actually difficult, without cheating by adding cheap one hit kill enemies.

The game now has a world screen, so you can visit any world you want from the start and each world has it's own sets of levels and boss fights. The boss fights are overall slightly easier and so is the main game. In the first game it felt like you needed a few of the hidden characters to help you finish the game, but honestly 2 is so easy, you can do it with the plain nerd, with little to no difficulty. 

There is of course difficult parts, especially the final set of levels which gave me quite a lot of trouble when I first played them, but overall I really found the game quite easy and a lot of fun to go through. It took me roughly 4 hours to finish the entire game and hunt for collectibles, but there's definitely more value if you go for a 100%. 

Verdict:

Angry Video Game Nerd 2: ASSimilation is an improvement over the first game in almost every way (sorry the soundtrack is better in the first one). I had a blast going through it and it's another nerd adventure for you to enjoy if you're a fan of The Nerd. If you liked the first game, you're definitely gonna like the sequel and even if you disliked the first one, this one is much better, so definitely consider giving it a shot.

Final Rating:
8.5/10

Pros:
+ Level Design is a much bigger improvement
+ Gameplay is fun and new additions really spice things up
+ Difficult, but fair

Cons:
- Short
- Soundtrack, while good, is nowhere near as good as the first one
